title: service fade probe log
content:
Purpose:
Quick hands-on notes for the \"service fade\" probe: a targeted load pattern intended to surface slow-onset degradation (minutes-long SLO drift) when a mixture of streaming and short requests compete for GPU KV cache and small-batch fastpath. Not a polished report — scratchpad for follow-ups.

Hypothesis:
- When a sustained low-rate background of long-context streaming (seq=2048) is combined with bursts of short-chat requests (seq=64, p50 tokens), the allocator + KV cache eviction policy will gradually increase tail latency for the short requests due to cold KV churn and partial kernel thrashing.

Environment:
- Cluster: 3x A100-80GB (shared pool, dedicated test tenancy)
- Serving binary: runtime-v2.3.1-experimental
- Model: open-llama-13b-fp16 (quant: fp16), also tried int8 later
- Loadgen: modified vbench (headless), client sim on 4 workers
- Config flags: continuous_batching=true, kv_cache_policy=LRU-windowed(90s), preemptive_eviction=false

Test plan:
1) Warm start: 10 minutes steady short-chat baseline (qps 40, concurrency 16). Record p50/p95/p99 and qps.
2) Inject streaming background: 5 long streams (each ~3rps but long seq) started at t=0 and sustained.
3) After 8 minutes, begin 30s spike trains of short-chat (qps=220) every 2 minutes for 30 minutes (to mimic intermittent load).
4) Observe rolling latency and KV hit rate. Collect traces and sample stacks for high-p99 spikes.

Key measurements (representative window)
- Baseline (no streams): qps=40, p50=28ms, p95=65ms, p99=180ms, kv_hit=0.98
- After streams (steady): qps(short)=40, p50=35ms, p95=90ms, p99=260ms, kv_hit=0.84
- During repeated spikes (after ~18m): qps(short)=180 burst, p50=45ms, p95=250ms, p99=1800ms, kv_hit=0.56

Observations / notes:
- KV hit rate correlates tightly with p95/p99. As hit rate drifts below ~0.7 the p99 explodes (>1.5s) for short requests even though avg token cost looks steady.
- Memory pressure: GPU mem free shows oscillation aligned with streaming checkpoint writes; not a full OOM but causes extra memcpy/GC cycles in the runtime.
- Preemptive_eviction=false seemed to worsen the slow drift; enabling preemptive_eviction cut the p99 by ~35% in a replay.
- INT8 run (same pattern) reduced absolute token compute but increased variance — smaller median but more tail: p99 spikes were similar magnitude, suggesting kernel scheduling and KV churn are dominant.

Quick sketch (ASCII) of KV hit vs p99 over time:
[time] kv_hit: 0.98 ---- 0.84 ---- 0.56
p99(ms):  180  --- 260  --- 1800  <--- aligned with repeated spikes

Preliminary conclusions:
- The slow-onset SLO degradation is primarily a caching/eviction interaction under interleaved long and short workloads, not raw compute saturation.
- Policies that coalesce and pin short-request KV slices or prioritize KV residency for short lanes look promising.
- Preemptive eviction + short-request pin pool reduced tail in quick replays; need a controlled A/B to confirm.

Next experiments TODO (short list):
- A/B: enable pin_pool_for_short=true (size 256MB) vs baseline, run 2x 1h windows.
- Trace-level correlation: capture kernel launch queues + nvlink memcpy timelines around p99 spikes.
- Test with model chunking (split long streams across 2 smaller contexts) to see if reducing single-stream KV size helps.
- Try hybrid quant: keys in int8, values fp16, to save KV mem without hurting compute kernel choices.

Open questions / gotchas:
- Is the LRU-windowed eviction implementation using host-side timers? There was a jitter in eviction timestamps which may explain periodic collapses — ask infra for telemetry hooks.
- Need a repro harness that deterministically reproduces the 18m tipping point (right now it varies 12–25m depending on tiny seed differences).

Notes to self:
- Upload sample trace + pcap to the linked PR and reference JIRA.
- Sync with Mira on preemptive_eviction flag semantics before large A/B.
- If we can pin short-request keys cheaply, we should see tail drop without cost regression; design tradeoff doc needed for node-level pin budgets.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to nicer runbook if A/B confirms.
